name: local-missed-requirement
about: A local job whose earlier leads often missed a hard requirement or gave a wrong number.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 44 were called and 25 were reached.
21 of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days did not meet a hard requirement of the opening.
9 of the 44 ad leads we called in the last 28 days had a wrong number.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the stated experience requirement and now run longer lanes or local work with uneven hours. They want hourly pay and a Monday to Friday week, home daily. They stop on an ad that names the requirement and the touch freight plainly.

angles.idea: Lead with the plain terms of the job: Class A, the stated experience requirement and touch freight, before any benefit.
angles.proof: The opening is Class A local delivery, states a years requirement and involves touch freight.
angles.why: A large share of recent leads failed a hard requirement, so stating it up front should screen them out. No ad results by hook are on the sheet, so this is unmeasured.

angles.idea: Lead with the hourly pay rate for local Class A delivery, with the experience requirement stated beside it.
angles.proof: The opening pays the stated hourly rate.
angles.why: Hourly pay is the clearest term the job has and sets it apart from per-mile work. Pairing it with the requirement answers the unqualified leads. Nothing is measured yet by hook.

angles.idea: Lead with the week the job gives: Monday to Friday, home daily, with health insurance as the supporting line.
angles.proof: The opening offers home daily, a Monday to Friday schedule and health insurance.
angles.why: The schedule is what a local job offers that longer lanes do not. No earlier results by hook exist, so this rests only on the job's facts.

angles.idea: Lead with the day cab as the sign of local work, parked at the end of the shift, with touch freight named.
angles.proof: The job runs a day cab on local delivery, is home daily and involves touch freight.
angles.why: The day cab shows at a glance that this is local work, and naming touch freight keeps it honest. The job has only this equipment fact, so it is the thinnest angle and unmeasured.
